Hey grads! 🗣️ You’re almost there; here are a few quick reminders before the big day:

📱 Make sure your guests have their tickets in hand & download theirs BEFORE arriving. Cell service can be spotty around the stadium.

🚶 Participating in the Walk Across Campus? Be at the Wren Yard by 4:30 p.m. Friday. The walk starts promptly at 5 p.m.

👟 Wear comfortable shoes (seriously). It’ll be hot and humid, and there’s a LOT of walking. Heels are not your friend.

🎒 Pack light — phones and cameras only. A clear bag policy is in effect, and refillable water bottles, umbrellas, signs, balloons, and outside food are not permitted.

🚗 Plan for heavy traffic + arrive early. Gates and parking open at 4 p.m.

🌧 Weather plan: If needed, the ceremony moves indoors to Kaplan Arena. Gold tickets work for both venues; green tickets are valid for Zable Stadium only.

Most importantly—soak it all in. You earned this. 💚💛 

#williamandmary | #wmGrad | #wm2026

COLL 100 courses invite first-year students to explore big ideas and new perspectives through hands-on learning across disciplines. In Photomania, taught by Prof. Eliot Dudik, students examine photography as an intersection of technology, history, and human experience. For one recent project, the class documented a walk through campus using their phones before assembling the images into a massive collaborative collage inspired by memory, movement, and place.

Like many COLL 100 courses, Photomania encourages students to think critically, communicate creatively, and engage beyond the traditional classroom experience. Follow more at @williamandmary_photo 📸

On the 11th hour of the 11th day of the 11th month, a William & Mary student veteran slowly tolls the Wren Bell to commemorate Armistice Day—the original inspiration for Veterans Day.
 
This year, as the Wren Bell rang in unison with others across the nation, we paused to honor the service and sacrifice of all our veterans. We are incredibly proud of our student veterans and the entire W&M military community. Thank you for your service.

William & Mary has been designated an “R1” research institution by the Carnegie Classification system.
 
“This classification is a well-deserved milestone for our outstanding students and faculty,” said Provost Peggy Agouris. “It reflects our university’s commitment to innovative research and scholarship and exemplifies William & Mary’s mission as a research university dedicated to advancing knowledge and making a meaningful impact. 
 
With the university's ascension to R1 status, William & Mary is entering a new era of research excellence and impact, strengthening the ability of the faculty to attract large-scale competitive funding, expand interdisciplinary collaboration across the liberal arts and sciences, and advance knowledge in ways that address pressing societal and global challenges.

👉🔗 Read the full story at the link in our bio.
